q: The concept of determining modes for the Navier-Stokes equations says that the long-time behavior is determined by a finite number of Fourier modes N_d. The estimate for N_d is:
opts: N_d ∼ Re³/² or G^{2/3} (depending on dimension and norm)
exp: Foias-Prodi-Ladyzhenskaya theorem: if two solutions agree on the first N Fourier modes for all t, they are asymptotically identical, for N above a threshold N_d ∼ G^{2/3}. This is the number of 'determining modes' and relates to the attractor dimension.
